title: Compiler Command Line Reference
summary: Detailed reference for the Thrust compiler command line flags in v0.2.0.
overview: This section explains the command line flags available in Thrust Compiler v0.2.0 and gives a practical view of what each group of options is for.
Use it when you need a stable reference for compilation, linking, diagnostics, emitted outputs, or target selection in this archived release.
Each category groups related flags together and includes accepted values, examples, and notes based on the published v0.2.0 command line snapshot.

categories.title: General Commands
categories.summary: Entry-point commands for help, version, and diagnostic explanations.
categories.intro: These commands do not primarily configure code generation. They are used to inspect the compiler, request help, or explain diagnostics.

flags.name: -h
flags.description: Show the compiler help message.
details: Without an extra topic, this prints the full top-level command line help.
With a supported topic, it prints the focused help for that flag family instead of the generic overview.
notes: Topics are optional. Unsupported topics fall back to the general help output.
This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -v
flags.description: Print the compiler version and exit.
details: This does not start a compilation pipeline. It only prints the current compiler version string.

flags.name: --explain
flags.description: Show the explanation for a compiler error or warning code.
details: Use this when you already have a diagnostic code and want the longer explanation text.
The accepted value is a compiler issue code such as an error or warning identifier.
notes: The exact available codes depend on the compiler version.
This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

categories.title: Linkage Flags
categories.summary: Flags that select or configure the external linker toolchain.
categories.intro: These flags control which external C or C++ compiler participates in the linking stage and what raw arguments it receives.

flags.name: -link-with-clang
flags.description: Specify the external Clang binary used for the linking stage.
details: This forces the linker driver to use a specific Clang executable instead of automatic detection.
It is useful when more than one LLVM or Clang toolchain is installed on the machine.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -link-with-gcc
flags.description: Specify the external GCC binary used for the linking stage.
details: This selects GCC as the external linking compiler.
Use it when you want GCC-specific linking behavior or when GCC is the available host linker toolchain.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -cc-args
flags.description: Forward raw arguments to the active external C or C++ linking compiler.
details: This is the escape hatch for linker or C compiler options that do not have a first-class Thrust flag.
Arguments can be separated by spaces or semicolons inside the raw string.
notes: This value is treated as a raw argument list and is split by the CLI preprocessor.
This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

categories.title: Compiler Flags
categories.summary: Core compilation, backend, target, JIT, ABI, and debug flags.
categories.intro: These flags shape the actual compilation pipeline: targets, outputs, optimization, JIT execution, standard library resolution, ABI behavior, and debug information.

flags.name: -build-dir
flags.description: Set the directory used for generated compiler artifacts.
details: Use this when you want emitted files, intermediates, and temporary build outputs to live outside the default location.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -tools-dir
flags.description: Set the compiler tools directory used to find external helper tools.
details: This points the compiler at a tools root that expands what it can discover automatically during the pipeline.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -target
flags.description: Set the target architecture.
details: Use this when the desired architecture is enough and you do not need to spell a full target triple.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -target-triple
flags.description: Set the full target triple used for code generation and linking decisions.
details: The target triple controls operating system, architecture, vendor, and ABI assumptions in one place.
Prefer this over `-target` when cross-compiling or when the platform details matter.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -cpu
flags.description: Select the CPU model used for optimization and code generation tuning.
details: This helps the backend emit code for a specific processor family rather than a generic architecture.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -cpu-enable-features
flags.description: Enable specific CPU features in addition to the CPU baseline.
details: Use this when you want to turn on a small set of backend features without replacing the whole feature list.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -cpu-disable-features
flags.description: Disable specific CPU features from the active configuration.
details: This is useful when the selected CPU baseline is too aggressive for the actual deployment environment.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -cpu-features
flags.description: Replace the CPU feature set with an explicit signed list.
details: This gives direct low-level control over the backend feature string.
Use it when you want an explicit allow and deny list rather than incremental enable or disable flags.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -emit
flags.description: Emit one selected compilation artifact instead of performing only the default end-to-end flow.
details: Use emission when you want a file output such as LLVM IR, assembler, object code, tokens, or AST snapshots.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -print
flags.description: Print one selected compilation representation to standard output.
details: This is the text-output twin of `-emit`.
Use it for inspection, debugging, or piping compiler output into another tool.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -opt
flags.description: Choose the optimization level.
details: Higher levels generally trade compilation time for more aggressive optimization.
Use size-oriented levels when output size matters more than raw performance.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -stop-at
flags.description: Stop the pipeline after a selected compiler stage.
details: This is useful for debugging the compiler pipeline and inspecting partial outputs.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -reloc-model
flags.description: Select how the backend handles relocations and external symbol references.
details: This affects generated machine code and the way addresses are represented.
Use PIC-related modes when the output must be position independent.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -code-model
flags.description: Choose the backend code model.
details: The code model influences assumptions about code and data placement in the address space.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -macos-version
flags.description: Set the macOS SDK or deployment version used for Apple targets.
details: Use this when you need the generated output to match a specific macOS deployment baseline.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -ios-version
flags.description: Set the iOS SDK or deployment version used for Apple mobile targets.
details: This matters when targeting Apple mobile environments and their deployment constraints.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -cuda-version
flags.description: Set the NVIDIA CUDA version used for CUDA-oriented compilation flows.
details: This lets the compiler adapt CUDA-related ABI or backend expectations for a particular CUDA release.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -jit
flags.description: Enable the JIT execution mode.
details: With JIT enabled, the compiler prepares the program for in-process execution instead of only generating files.
notes: Some other JIT flags only make sense when this flag is already active.

flags.name: -jit-libc
flags.description: Set the C runtime used by the JIT execution flow.
details: Use this when the JIT runtime must link against a specific C runtime library.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -jit-link
flags.description: Add an extra shared library for JIT execution.
details: This lets the JIT loader resolve external symbols from additional libraries.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -jit-entry
flags.description: Set the entry point symbol used by JIT execution.
details: Use this when the executed function is not the default `main`.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -jit-args
flags.description: Pass arguments to the program executed through the JIT runtime.
details: Arguments are passed through the JIT configuration rather than through the host shell after compilation.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -abi
flags.description: Select the ABI used for code generation.
details: The ABI affects calling conventions, data passing rules, and interoperability with external code.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -mode
flags.description: Select the compiler features mode.
details: Stable mode limits the language surface to stable features.
Unstable mode enables experimental or incomplete features.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -std
flags.description: Set the standard library root path.
details: Use this when the compiler should resolve the standard library from a non-default location.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -std-version
flags.description: Set the standard library version to use.
details: This helps the compiler resolve the expected versioned standard library snapshot.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: -dbg
flags.description: Enable generation of debug information.
details: This turns on backend debug info emission such as DWARF data where supported.

flags.name: -dbg-for-inlining
flags.description: Emit debug information optimized for inlined functions.
details: Use this when debugging optimized builds where inlining would otherwise hide useful location information.

flags.name: -dbg-for-profiling
flags.description: Emit extra debug information for source-level profiling tools.
details: This helps profilers map optimized machine code back to the original source more accurately.

flags.name: -dbg-dwarf-version
flags.description: Set the DWARF version used for debug information.
details: Use this when your debugger or platform requires a specific DWARF generation.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: --disable-abi
flags.description: Disable ABI detection and ABI-specific code generation behavior.
details: This can be useful for debugging or for niche targets where automatic ABI handling gets in the way.

flags.name: --denormal-floating-point-behavior
flags.description: Control how denormal floating-point values are handled for general floating-point operations.
details: This affects how the backend treats denormal values and therefore can change numerical edge-case behavior.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: --denormal-floating-point-32-bits-behavior
flags.description: Control how denormal 32-bit floating-point values are handled.
details: This is the 32-bit specific counterpart of the general denormal floating-point behavior flag.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: --symbol-linkage-strategy
flags.description: Choose the strategy used when symbol linkages need to be merged or reconciled.
details: This matters when the backend has to reason about multiple declarations of the same symbol.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: --stack-protector
flags.description: Enable stack protection instrumentation.
details: This inserts stack state protection intended to make some classes of memory corruption harder to exploit.

flags.name: --sanitizer
flags.description: Enable one selected sanitizer runtime and its instrumentation.
details: Sanitizers add runtime checks and diagnostics for memory issues, threading bugs, or related classes of problems.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: --no-sanitize
flags.description: Disable specific sanitizer subfeatures or code emission details.
details: Use this to narrow or tune the effect of an active sanitizer configuration.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: --opt-passes
flags.description: Pass a custom LLVM optimization pass list.
details: Use this when the default optimization pipeline is not enough and you want to control LLVM pass selection directly.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: --modificator-passes
flags.description: Pass a custom modificator optimization pass list.
details: This lets you tune the pass set used by the compiler-specific modificator stage.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: --target-triple-darwin-variant
flags.description: Set the Darwin target variant triple.
details: Use this when a Darwin target needs its variant triple spelled out separately from the main target triple.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: --enable-ansi-color
flags.description: Enable ANSI color formatting in diagnostics output.
details: This is useful when the compiler runs in terminals or logs that preserve ANSI escape sequences.

categories.title: Disable Compiler Flags
categories.summary: Flags that switch off selected backend, math, sanitizer, or optimization behaviors.
categories.intro: These flags turn off optional behavior that would otherwise be active, either by default or because of another active mode.

flags.name: --disable-frame-pointer
flags.description: Omit frame pointer emission regardless of optimization level.
details: This can reduce overhead or follow platform-specific conventions, but it can also make debugging and stack walking harder.

flags.name: --disable-uwtable
flags.description: Omit unwind table emission.
details: This can reduce output size, but it may hurt exception handling support or stack tracing quality.

flags.name: --disable-direct-access-external-data
flags.description: Force external data references to be accessed indirectly instead of directly.
details: This changes how the backend reaches external data symbols and can matter for relocation or platform constraints.

flags.name: --disable-rtlib-got
flags.description: Disable the runtime library dependency on the Global Offset Table.
details: The original help text describes this as useful for some ARM non-PIC situations.

flags.name: --disable-safe-trapping-math
flags.description: Allow trapping math operations instead of forcing safer behavior.
details: This mainly affects floating-point code paths where the backend would otherwise avoid trap-prone behavior.

flags.name: --disable-safe-math
flags.description: Disable safe integer math behavior.
details: This allows overflow-oriented or less constrained math behavior at the cost of stronger guarantees.

flags.name: --disable-default-optimization
flags.description: Disable the default optimization work that would otherwise happen even without an explicit optimization flag.
details: This is the spelling shown in the local v0.2.0 release snapshot.

flags.name: --disable-all-sanitizers
flags.description: Disable all sanitizers.
details: Use this to clear sanitizer instrumentation globally for the current compilation.

flags.name: --disable-all-cpu-features
flags.description: Disable all CPU feature toggles.
details: This clears CPU feature assumptions back toward a minimal baseline.

categories.title: Warning Compiler Flags
categories.intro: These flags affect how warning diagnostics are emitted and filtered.

flags.name: --disable-warnings
flags.description: Disable selected warning codes.
details: Use this when a known warning is intentionally triggered and you want to silence it locally for the current build.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: --disable-all-warnings
flags.description: Disable all general and specific warnings.
details: This suppresses warning diagnostics broadly and should be used carefully.

categories.title: Other Compiler Flags
categories.summary: Quality-of-life, cleanup, diagnostic export, and discovery flags.
categories.intro: These flags do not fit the core target or codegen categories. They mostly help with inspection, cleanup, exports, and tool discovery.

flags.name: --copy-output-to-clipboard
flags.description: Copy the printable compiler output to the system clipboard.
details: This only makes sense when a `-print` flag is also active and the platform clipboard integration is available.

flags.name: --debug-clang-command
flags.description: Display the generated Clang command used during linking.
details: This helps inspect or debug the external command the compiler is about to run.

flags.name: --debug-gcc-command
flags.description: Display the generated GCC command used during linking.
details: This is the GCC counterpart of `--debug-clang-command`.

flags.name: --export-compiler-errors
flags.description: Export compiler error diagnostics to files.
details: Use this when you want diagnostics persisted instead of only printed to the terminal.

flags.name: --export-compiler-warnings
flags.description: Export compiler warning diagnostics to files.
details: This is useful for build automation or post-processing warning results.

flags.name: --export-diagnostics-path
flags.description: Set the directory used for exported diagnostics.
details: Use this with diagnostic export flags to control where the compiler writes its files.
notes: This flag accepts a value separated by a space, `=` or `:`.

flags.name: --clean-exported-diagnostics
flags.description: Clean the exported diagnostics directory.
details: This removes or resets previously exported diagnostic files before or after a compilation workflow.

flags.name: --clean-build
flags.description: Clean the compiler build directory.
details: Use this to remove accumulated compilation artifacts.

flags.name: --clean-tokens
flags.description: Clean the directory that stores lexical token outputs.
details: This is mostly useful when using token emission or token printing workflows.

flags.name: --clean-assembler
flags.description: Clean the directory that stores emitted assembler files.
details: This helps keep emitted assembler output tidy between builds.

flags.name: --clean-llvm-ir
flags.description: Clean the directory that stores emitted LLVM IR files.
details: Use this when repeatedly emitting IR and you want a clean output directory.

flags.name: --clean-llvm-bitcode
flags.description: Clean the directory that stores emitted LLVM bitcode files.
details: This is the bitcode-specific cleanup flag.

flags.name: --clean-objects
flags.description: Clean the directory that stores emitted object files.
details: Use this when object file output should be reset before a new build.

flags.name: --dump-compiler-version
flags.description: Write the compiler version into `COMPILER_VERSION.txt`.
details: This exports the version string to a flat text file in the working directory.

flags.name: --no-obfuscate-archive-names
flags.description: Disable file-name obfuscation for archive names.
details: The original help text notes that this does not apply to the final build output.

flags.name: --no-obfuscate-ir
flags.description: Disable name obfuscation in emitted IR output.
details: This is useful when emitted IR should stay easier to read or diff.

flags.name: --print-targets
flags.description: Print the supported targets.
details: Use this to inspect which targets are currently known by the compiler build.

flags.name: --print-supported-cpus
flags.description: Print the supported CPUs for the current target.
details: This helps choose a valid value for `-cpu`.

flags.name: --print-host-target-triple
flags.description: Print the host target triple.
details: This reports the native triple of the machine running the compiler.

flags.name: --print-opt-passes
flags.description: Print the optimization passes available through `--opt-passes`.
details: This is a discovery flag for users who want to build a custom pass list.
